clauses.reason: The ordering sentence amends sections 303 and 604 of EO 10480. EO 12919 section 904(a)(11) supersedes or revokes EO 12773 except that part of the order that amends section 604 of EO 10480; section 904(a)(3) of the same order supersedes or revokes EO 10480 itself ("(3) Executive Order No. 10480 of August 14, 1953 (18 FR 4939)."). Section 303 part: ended by the express supersession. Section 604 part: the carve-out kept it only as an amendment of EO 10480, whose text was revoked the same day, so it has no object after 1994-06-03. Effective date: EO 12919 states none for section 904, so its signing date applies.

research_rationale:
EO 12773 of September 26, 1991 (Amending Executive Order No. 10480), read in full in the held Federal Register text (56 FR 49387, Federal Register of September 30, 1991; machine-extracted text layer). Identity: number, date and subject agree with the census register row (1991-09-26). The order transfers Defense Production Act responsibilities of the General Services Administration to the Department of Defense by amending section 303 of EO 10480 (Administrator of General Services replaced by Secretary of Defense) and section 604 of EO 10480 (General Services Administration replaced by Department of Defense, and Administrator of General Services replaced by Secretary of Defense). The order states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. Under the owner's strike-and-insert ruling (2026-10-21) an amending clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends; the amendment is therefore not exhausted on signing. EO 10480 was superseded or revoked by EO 12919 (signed 1994-06-03; 59 FR 29525, Federal Register of June 7, 1994) in section 904(a)(3), and EO 12919 section 904(a)(11) supersedes or revokes EO 12773 except that part that amends section 604 of EO 10480. Both parts therefore end on the same date: the section 303 part by the express supersession of EO 12773, and the section 604 part because its parent, EO 10480, was revoked in the same order on the same day. EO 12919 has no delayed-effective-date wording for section 904, so the date is its signing date, 1994-06-03. The dossier has one clause (the whole order) which covers the single ordering sentence. Searches: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML; Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts) were chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no scope warning. Machine hits for this order: current-law:usc 0, current-law:ecfr 0, later-events:ofr_catalog 3. The packet's by-number scan of held order texts (LOOKUPS) was read for this order; two held texts cite this number, this order and EO 12919.

savings.reason: Actions taken under EO 10480 as amended by EO 12773 (delegations and functions exercised by the Secretary of Defense in place of the Administrator of General Services) are accrued effects. EO 12919 keeps earlier delegations, rules and other actions in effect except as inconsistent or later amended or revoked, so savings of that kind rest on EO 12919, not on EO 12773.
